_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Sri Lanka covering ancient Anuradhapura/Polonnaruwa kingdoms, introduction of Buddhism (Mahinda, 3rd century BCE), Sinhalese chronicles (Mahavamsa), Tamil kingdoms (Jaffna), Portuguese/Dutch/British colonial rule, independence 1948, Sinhalese-Tamil tensions, Black July riots 1983, civil war 1983-2009 (Tamil Tigers/LTTE), Rajapaksa dynastic rule, Easter bombings 2019, economic collapse 2022, and Aragalaya protests.

religion.note: Buddhism special status in constitution; Sinhalese overwhelmingly Buddhist; Tamils overwhelmingly Hindu (north/east) or Christian (some); Muslims (Moors, Malays) Sunni; 969 Movement (Buddhist extremism); temple/dagoba culture (Tooth Relic, Kandy)

ethnic_groups.name: Sinhalese
ethnic_groups.notes: Indo-Aryan; Buddhist; Sinhala language; politically dominant; southern/central/western; 'sons of the soil' ideology (Mahavamsa); Kandyan vs low-country divide; SLFP/SLPP support base

ethnic_groups.name: Sri Lankan Tamil
ethnic_groups.notes: Dravidian; Hindu/Christian; northern/eastern provinces (Jaffna, Batticaloa); 'traditional homeland' claim; LTTE insurgency base; caste (Vellalar upper); minority grievances since 1956 Sinhala Only Act

ethnic_groups.name: Sri Lankan Moor (Muslim)
ethnic_groups.notes: Tamil-speaking Muslims; Arab/South Indian descent; merchants; eastern province; distinct from Tamils; targeted in 2019 Easter bombings backlash; UNP traditionally

ethnic_groups.name: Indian Tamil
ethnic_groups.notes: Brought by British (1820s+) for tea/rubber plantations; hill country (Kandy); stateless until 1980s-2000s; poor; CWC party

ethnic_groups.name: Burgher
ethnic_groups.notes: Eurasian (Portuguese/Dutch mixed); English-speaking; elite; mostly emigrated post-independence

ethnic_groups.name: Malay, Veddha, Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Malays (Java/Southeast Asia, colonial-era); Veddha (indigenous, ~1,000, forest-dwellers); Chinese (small merchant community)

country_profile.notes_unique: Civil War 1983-2009 (~100,000 dead); LTTE (Tamil Tigers, Prabhakaran, suicide bombers invented); Black July 1983 (anti-Tamil pogrom); Sinhalese-Tamil ethnic conflict; 2004 tsunami (35,000 dead); Rajapaksa family dynastic rule; 2022 economic collapse (default, Aragalaya/Go Gota Go protests); Easter bombings 2019 (ISIS-inspired, ~270 dead); Ceylon tea; Adam's Peak; Sigiriya rock fortress (UNESCO); 'teardrop of India'; Chinese debt-trap (Hambantota port)

natural_resources.notes: World's top gem producer (sapphires); graphite mining historically significant; ilmenite/rutile sand deposits.

military.notes: Large military relative to population; expanded during civil war (1983-2009); increasingly close ties with China (Hambantota port lease); traditional Non-Aligned Movement member.

infrastructure.notes: Central Expressway modernizing road network; British-era railway system; Colombo Port City (Port City Colombo) $1.4B Chinese-backed reclamation project.

climate_environment.notes: Biodiversity hotspot; Western Ghats/Sri Lanka hotspot; 2004 Asian tsunami killed 35,000+; rich coral reefs; elephant-human conflict.

debt_aid.notes: Sovereign default April 2022; IMF $2.9B Extended Fund Facility; debt restructuring negotiations with bilateral creditors; Chinese debt trap concerns (Hambantota).

education.notes: Free education from primary through university (since 1945); high literacy; low tertiary enrollment due to limited university places; competitive A-level system.

diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Outward migration focused (domestic workers to Gulf)
diaspora_migration.notes: Remittances critical lifeline during 2022 crisis; Tamil diaspora politically active (especially Canada/UK); Gulf worker migration dominant.

digital_economy.notes: IT/BPO sector growing; ~$1.2B IT exports annually; Colombo startup ecosystem emerging; mobile penetration high.

geography.terrain: Coastal plains in north; central highlands with tea plantations; dry zone in east/north
geography.notes: Island nation (Pearl of the Indian Ocean); Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu) nearly connects to India; strategic location on major east-west shipping routes.

economy_extended.notes: Severe economic crisis 2022 (sovereign default); IMF $2.9B bailout; foreign reserves collapsed; shortages of fuel/medicine/food; debt restructuring underway; recovery fragile.

health.notes: Free universal healthcare since 1951; strong public health outcomes despite low spending; malaria eliminated 2016 (WHO certified).

food_agriculture.notes: Ceylon tea world-famous (3rd largest producer); true cinnamon (Cinnamomum verum) native here; rice self-sufficiency policy; organic farming push.

energy.notes: No oil/gas reserves; hydro backbone; solar capacity growing rapidly; 2022 crisis caused fuel shortages and rolling blackouts; renewable energy target 70% by 2030.

transport.notes: Colombo port major transshipment hub on East-West shipping route; Hambantota leased to China for 99 years (debt-for-equity).

tourism.notes: Tourism recovering post-crisis and COVID; 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites; popular for wildlife, beaches, heritage, and tea trails.

human_rights_gender.notes: Low female political representation despite high female education; PTA (Prevention of Terrorism Act) criticized; post-war accountability for Tamil civilian deaths unresolved.

security_stability.notes: Civil war ended 2009 (LTTE defeated); 2019 Easter bombings killed 269; Aragalaya protests 2022 ousted President Rajapaksa; Tamil reconciliation incomplete.

legal_system.notes: Complex plural legal system; Roman-Dutch general law; Kandyan law for Kandyan Sinhalese; Thesawalamai for Jaffna Tamils; MMDA for Muslims; PTA controversial.

cultural_heritage.film_industry: Sinhala cinema ('Rekava' 1956 landmark); small but critically acclaimed
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Vibrant but under pressure; attacks on journalists; media in Sinhala, Tamil, English
cultural_heritage.notes: World's first female PM (Sirimavo Bandaranaike 1960); 2500+ years of documented civilization; Sigiriya is iconic UNESCO site.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.

current_leader.name: Anura Kumara Dissanayake
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: NPP/JVP (Marxist); first leftist president; elected after economic crisis; anti-corruption; broke Rajapaksa/UNP duopoly; 'Compass' symbol; former JVP leader

former_leaders.name: Ranil Wickremesinghe
former_leaders.notes: UNP; sixth-time PM before president; took over after Rajapaksa fled (2022 protests); IMF bailout; unpopular austerity; lost 2024 election; nephew of J.R. Jayewardene

former_leaders.name: Gotabaya Rajapaksa
former_leaders.notes: SLPP; younger brother of Mahinda; former Defence Secretary; ended civil war (2009); organic farming disaster (fertilizer ban, crop failures); forex crisis; fuel/food shortages; Aragalaya protests; fled to Maldives July 2022; resigned; first president forced out by protests

former_leaders.name: Maithripala Sirisena
former_leaders.notes: SLFP defector; defeated Mahinda Rajapaksa; 'good governance' coalition with Ranil; Easter bombings 2019 (intelligence failure); political chaos; constitutional crisis 2018

former_leaders.name: Mahinda Rajapaksa
former_leaders.notes: UPFA/SLFP; ended civil war 2009 (defeated LTTE, war crimes allegations); Sinhalese nationalist; China tilt; Hambantota port; corruption; family nepotism (brothers in cabinet); lost 2015 election; later PM under brother Gotabaya

former_leaders.name: Chandrika Kumaratunga
former_leaders.notes: SLFP; first female president; daughter of Sirimavo/S.W.R.D. Bandaranaike; lost eye in suicide bombing 1999; peace talks with LTTE failed; authoritarian streak

former_leaders.name: Ranasinghe Premadasa
former_leaders.notes: UNP; assassinated by LTTE suicide bomber; Indian intervention (IPKF) withdrawal; Sinhalese-JVP insurgency crackdown

former_leaders.name: J.R. Jayewardene
former_leaders.notes: UNP; first executive president; 1978 constitution (French-style, executive powers); Black July riots 1983 (under his watch); open economy; IPKF invited 1987; authoritarian; 'Yankee Dickie'

former_leaders.name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike
former_leaders.notes: SLFP; world's first female PM; widow of S.W.R.D.; socialist policies; 1971 JVP uprising crushed; 1972 republic (Ceylon → Sri Lanka); mother of Chandrika; later PM again 1994-2000; died 2000

former_leaders.name: S.W.R.D. Bandaranaike
former_leaders.notes: SLFP founder; 'Sinhala Only Act' 1956 (Tamil grievances began); assassinated by Buddhist monk; husband of Sirimavo; father of Chandrika

910.name: Prehistoric and Early Settlement
910.description: The extraordinarily ancient human presence in Sri Lanka, the Balangoda Man remains, the Veddah aboriginal people, and the island's pre-Buddhist cultures in one of the world's oldest continuous human habitations.

sub_clusters.description: The Homo sapiens remains from Fa Hien Cave (one of the earliest outside Africa), the Balangoda Man skeletal remains, early stone-tool cultures, and the Veddah aboriginal people as descendants of the earliest settlers.
key_events: Fa Hien Cave yields evidence of Homo sapiens occupation dating to 125,000 years ago — among the earliest outside Africa
